newsitem.title: USA: Florida bill sets limit on who can appeal bonds.
newsitem.headline: Florida bill sets limit on who can appeal bonds.

text.p: A Florida Senate committee has approved a bill that would allow bond validations to be appealed only by those who would help repay the debt.
The proposal (SB2138) was approved Tuesday by the Senate's Government Reform and Oversight Committee.
Under current Florida law, any "interested party" can appeal a bond validation.

"We have recommended and basically stated that unless you are a person who is required to pay additional money as a result of the debt, you have no standing," said Joe Lombardi, chief legislative analyst for the committee.
"What we want to do is make sure we don't unnecessarily tie things up in court," Lombardi said.

The bill was sponsored by Sen. William "Doc" Myers, R-Stuart. It was drafted at the request of constituents in Port St. Lucie, where a $8.65 million water-sewer bond issue was delayed for more than two years by legal appeals.

The bond issue involved a special assessment and was considered routine until a man who was not a property owner, paid no city taxes and lived outside the assement district appealed the bond validation.
The case went all the way to the Florida Supreme Court, which upheld the bonds, and later denied the plantiffs' request for a re-hearing. The bonds were finally sold in March 1996.
